parole.testo: Borrowed from Proto-Finnic *kansa. Cognate with Livonian kōz.

parole.significato: boat (small vehicle for transporting people, goods, etc. on water)
parole.testo: Cognates include Lithuanian lai̇̃vas, dialectal lai̇̃vė, archaic lai̇̃va. The relationship by borrowing to Proto-Finnic *laiva (Finnish laiva “ship; nave”, Estonian laev, Livonian lōja) is also undisputed, leaving the question of which family had the word first. Traditionally considered a borrowing from Proto-Finnic *maa (“land, earth”) (compare Estonian maa, Finnish maa, Veps ma, Livonian mō); the meaning evolved from “earth, land” → “earth, fields close to a village, to (farm) houses” → “(farm) house.” This word was also re-borrowed into Proto-Finnic as *
